question: Can the NLP/MINLP engines publish a measured maximum_primal_violation into the shared result fields without guessing at residual semantics?

gap.verbatim: The nonlinear engines carry the same class of gap: src/api/engine_nonlinear.cpp never fills primal_report, and src/nlp/nlp_verifier.cpp folds bound violations into inequality_violation, so JSON maximum_primal_violation stays a defaulted 0 for NLP/MINLP results while diagnostics carry residuals under different names.
gap.prior_status: documented, not fixed - mapping those residual definitions onto the shared primal_report field would require a semantics decision (which residual equals which row violation)

decision.contract: docs/contracts/numerical-policy.md section 4, paragraph 'NLP/MINLP primal report mapping' (added in this change; no status, assurance or witness change, so the contract stays v3)

mapping.maximum_primal_violation: NlpFeasibilityReport.maximum_constraint_violation: max(0, g_i(x)) over inequality rows and |h_i(x)| over equality rows, recomputed from the user callbacks at the reported iterate (g/h are the rows on this path; there is no matrix activity)
mapping.maximum_variable_violation: NlpFeasibilityReport.maximum_bound_violation: the variable-bound form, measured in its own accumulator instead of being folded into the row side
mapping.maximum_integrality_violation: max |x_j - round(x_j)| over declared-integer variables at the same iterate; MINLP gates it against feasibility_tolerance, the SQP path reports it without gating (continuous engine)
mapping.passed: the engine gate verdict for that iterate: SQP = the 1e-6 feasibility verdict, MINLP = feasibility and integrality and objective-consistency, exactly original_verified

decision.attachment_rule: filled iff an iterate is attached to the result, the same rule as the linear engines; a result with no attached primal keeps the default-constructed report
decision.deliberately_not_filled: recomputed_objective / objective_difference stay at their defaults: the linear engines compare objectives in user-facing sense while the nonlinear engines' consistency check runs in normalized NLP space, and one shared field cannot carry both meanings (recorded, not guessed)
decision.unchanged: diagnostic nlp_inequality_violation keeps its historical definition (including the bound folding inside verify_nlp_solution); gates, tolerances and statuses are untouched

changes: include/markov_cero/nlp/nlp_verifier.hpp: NlpFeasibilityReport gains maximum_constraint_violation and maximum_bound_violation; maximum_violation = max of the two on every path, all three +inf on rejection
src/nlp/nlp_verifier.cpp: two accumulators replace the single folded one (identical maximum_violation value, max is order-independent)

src/api/engine_nonlinear.cpp: publish_primal_report on the three attach paths (SQP best-feasible attach, SQP KKT accept, MINLP incumbent); MINLP's integrality gate now derives from the same worst-residual measurement (equivalent verdict)

probe.method: same CLI and model file before and after: git stash of the fix, rebuild, run, restore, rebuild, run. probe.pre_fix_binary: HEAD build before this change (fix stashed)

invariants: passed == original_verified on every path that attaches a primal (asserted for SQP inequality, SQP equality and MINLP in nlp_primal_report)
MINLP: max(maximum_primal_violation, maximum_variable_violation) == diagnostic.primal_residual exactly, both from the same feasibility report
SQP: |diagnostic.primal_residual - maximum_primal_violation| <= 1e-15 on the inequality case (two computations of the same quantity at the same point)

split semantics pinned at chosen points: infeasible (0,0) -> constraint 1.5 / bound 0; (-1,2) -> constraint 0.5 / bound 1.0; equality at origin -> |h| = 2; dimension-mismatch rejection -> +inf on all three fields
row field equals max(0, 1.5 - (x0 + x1)) computed independently in the test on the reported iterate

verification.ctest: 122/122 on the rebuilt tree (121 prior + nlp_primal_report)
verification.cli: pre/post JSON captured above; statuses LocalStationary on both sides, verdicts unchanged

coverage_and_limits: attach paths exercised through api::solve_model: SQP KKT-accept (inequality and equality models) and MINLP incumbent success
the SQP best-feasible attach path (non-KKT exit with a feasibility-tolerated iterate) shares publish_primal_report but has no directed test: no public option forces that exit deterministically

the MINLP verification-failure attach (attached primal with passed=false) is reachable only when the incumbent fails its own gate; the engine constructs MinlpOptions internally, so api::solve_model cannot tighten the tolerance to force it - covered by code inspection, not by a test
recomputed_objective / objective_difference remain defaults on these paths (decision above)
no status, tolerance or gate changed: this is a reporting-only fix, so BENCH-01/02/03 verdicts are unaffected (the campaign harness reads neither field, benchmark-campaign.md section 8)
